title: Reworking QuerySet.order_by() validation dropped the ORDER_PATTERN regex check for strings containing a period, so a 'table.column'-style value from request input is passed through as raw SQL in ORDER BY.

findings.explanation: The change replaces a regex-based allowlist check (ORDER_PATTERN) with inline validation logic. The new code handles '?', '-' prefix, annotation names, extra names, and then delegates to names_to_path() which validates the field path against model metadata. This approach validates ordering items against actual model fields/annotations rather than allowing arbitrary strings through. No raw SQL string concatenation occurs; the ORM still uses parameterized queries. The validation is equivalent or stricter than the regex for legitimate field names.

This diff only modifies internal ORM query validation logic (order_by validation). It does not introduce or remove any authorization checks, does not expose new endpoints, and does not fetch objects by user-controlled IDs. No authorization-related code paths are touched.
